title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: GWEN'S GARAGE
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Gwen Hartley, an insurance claims adjuster from Lowell, Massachusetts.
For twenty-four years, she decided what was broken. Then her company decided she was too expensive.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: THE COUCH
segments.quote: A sad soul can kill you quicker, far quicker, than a germ.
segments.author: John Steinbeck
lines: They let her go on a video call. Her boss was on mute.
For three weeks, Gwen watched game shows in her robe.
Her sister Patty brought soup and a Steinbeck book, with one line circled:
A sad soul can kill you quicker, far quicker, than a germ.
So Gwen got dressed and opened her late dad's toolbox.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE SIGN-UP
segments.quote: Courage is the most important of all the virtues, because without courage you can't practice any other virtue consistently.
segments.author: Maya Angelou
lines: Dad fixed every lamp on the street for free. Gwen fixed a neighbor's lamp, then a waffle iron.
She dreamed of a free fix-it day at the library. But what if nobody came?
Patty's fridge magnet had Maya Angelou's words:
Courage is the most important of all the virtues, because without courage you can't practice any other virtue consistently.
Gwen booked the library room for Saturday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE TOASTER
segments.quote: What I cannot create, I do not understand.
segments.author: Richard Feynman
lines: Nine people came. The first brought a toaster that burned one side.
Gwen had no idea how it worked.
In Dad's toolbox was a note from the scientist Richard Feynman:
What I cannot create, I do not understand.
So she took the toaster apart, drew every piece, and rebuilt it. Twice. Golden toast.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE CREW
segments.quote: The most important measure of how good a game I played was how much better I'd made my teammates play.
segments.author: Bill Russell
lines: By spring, the line went out the door.
Sal, a retired TV repairman, offered to help. Gwen almost said no. She liked being the hero.
Sal quoted the basketball legend Bill Russell:
The most important measure of how good a game I played was how much better I'd made my teammates play.
So Gwen built a crew, and handed out screwdrivers and coffee.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE MUSIC BOX
segments.quote: It is the time you have wasted for your rose that makes your rose so important.
segments.author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
lines: Then Mr. Kowalski, a quiet widower, brought a four-dollar music box.
It played his late wife's favorite song. It had been silent for a year.
It took three hours. Gwen thought of The Little Prince:
It is the time you have wasted for your rose that makes your rose so important.
When it played, Mr. Kowalski held it to his ear and smiled.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE OFFER
segments.quote: I don't like work—no man does—but I like what is in the work—the chance to find yourself.
segments.author: Joseph Conrad
lines: Then her old company called. Come back. Bigger desk.
Gwen remembered Joseph Conrad, in Heart of Darkness:
I don't like work—no man does—but I like what is in the work—the chance to find yourself.
She said no, thank you, and opened Hartley Fix-It in Dad's garage.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Get up. Be brave. Take it apart. Lift your team. Take your time. Find yourself.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Get up. Be brave. Take it apart. Lift your team. Take your time. Find yourself.
I fixed my own toaster once. Now it sends smoke signals.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
